document_metadata.document_title: Kern County Development Standards — Division Four: Standards for Drainage (metro co-permittee basis)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Drainage facilities designed for Intermediate Storm Design Discharge (ISDD ≈ 10-year) and Capital Storm Design Discharge (CSDD ≈ 100-year). Retention basins (sumps) and detention basins sized for design ponding depth/volume per Kern County standards; off-site CSDD/ISDD mitigation required for development.
approved_bmp_categories: Closed conduit systems and catch basins

Retention basins shall not be permitted unless it can be demonstrated, to the satisfaction of the Director, that the basin will completely drain the design volume within seven (7) days.
RETENTION BASIN: is a terminal storm water facility for the storage of runoff. Commonly referred to as a sump.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Kern County Division Four drainage standards used for Bakersfield metro / co-permittee coverage. City of Bakersfield may publish a separate Subdivision/Engineering Design Manual — prefer swapping if a durable city PDF is found. Pipeline excerpt repair removed 1 unlocated citation(s).

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Kern County Division Four focuses on flood/quantity (ISDD ≈ 10-year, CSDD ≈ 100-year). Retention (sump) volume uses ISDD five-day rainfall from NOAA Atlas 14 Vol. 6 per Engineering Bulletin 11-02, not a separate WQv depth in inches. Detention/retardation basins follow ISDD five-day hydrograph; LID BMPs and manufactured treatment are not addressed in the provided excerpts.
